reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be a complete finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure. Let f:E->R be globally twice continuously Frechet differentiable, let kappa,h be real and J be natural. Assume kappa>=1, J>=2, h>0 and, for every z,v in E,
  (1/(2kappa))||v||^2 <= D^2 f(z)[v,v] <= ||v||^2.
For each i in Fin(J)={0,...,J-1}, define
  t_i=(h/2)(1-cos((i/(J-1))pi)),
with real coercions in the quotient. Let ell_j be the actual real Lagrange cardinal polynomial at the defined nodes. Define exactly
  Lambda=sup{sum_j |ell_j(s)| : s in [0,h]},
  omega_ij=integral_0^{t_i} (t_i-s)ell_j(s) ds,
  b_j=integral_0^h ell_j(s) ds,
  c_j=integral_0^h (h-s)ell_j(s) ds.
These are ordinary real Lebesgue interval integrals and the supremum is the real supremum of the displayed image. If h^2 Lambda<=1, put a=exp(-h/2),sigma=sqrt(1-exp(-h)),and let Gamma=G x G be the independent product of two standard isotropic Gaussian probability laws G on E.
For an incoming phase state z=(X,P) in E x E and noise zeta=(u,v) in E x E, define the direct-gradient two-stage update by
  P0(z,zeta)=a P+sigma u,
  Y0_j(z,zeta)=X+t_j P0(z,zeta),
  Y1_i(z,zeta)=Y0_i(z,zeta)-sum_j omega_ij grad f(Y0_j(z,zeta)),
  Phi(z,zeta)=(X+h P0(z,zeta)-sum_j c_j grad f(Y1_j(z,zeta)),
               a(P0(z,zeta)-sum_j b_j grad f(Y1_j(z,zeta)))+sigma v).
All sums run over all J actual indices. Then Phi is jointly measurable in its incoming state and both noise coordinates. There exists a Markov kernel K from E x E to E x E,with probability output measures,satisfying for every incoming state z
  K(z)=(zeta -> Phi(z,zeta))_* Gamma.
In addition,for every pair of incoming states z,zprime and every common noise pair zeta in E x E,define the actual continuous linear operator
  H=(1/h) sum_j b_j integral_0^1 A(Y1_j(zprime,zeta)+u(Y1_j(z,zeta)-Y1_j(zprime,zeta))) du,
where A(v) is the Riesz operator of the genuine continuous bilinear form D^2 f(v),characterized by <A(v)r,s>=D^2 f(v)[r,s]. The integrals here are Bochner interval integrals with values in continuous real linear operators E->E. In particular the secant segment runs from the primed second-stage point to the unprimed one,and H is fixed by these integrals and weights,not a supplied certificate.
Write deltaX=z.1-zprime.1,deltaP=z.2-zprime.2,and d=toLp2(deltaX,deltaP) in the Euclidean phase space L=WithLp 2(E x E). This space uses coordinatewise vector operations and norm sqrt(||X||^2+||P||^2);toLp2 preserves the pair coordinates. Then simultaneously:
  H is symmetric: <Hr,s>=<r,Hs> for all r,s in E;
  (1/(2kappa))||v||^2 <= <Hv,v> <= ||v||^2 for every v in E;
  ||H||_operator <=1;
  there exists a continuous real linear R:L->L with ||R||_operator<=8 Lambda h^2 such that
    toLp2(Phi(z,zeta).1-Phi(zprime,zeta).1,
          Phi(z,zeta).2-Phi(zprime,zeta).2)
      = d+h toLp2(deltaP,-H(deltaX)-deltaP)+R(d).
The R witness is inside the universal quantification over z,zprime,zeta. It may therefore depend on the compared states and common noise,while its displayed operator-norm bound is uniform in those data. No single global R or measurable dependence of R on them is asserted. Both outputs use exactly the same noise pair. Norms of H use the induced E operator norm;the norm of R uses the stated Euclidean L2 phase norm rather than the default product max norm.
The conclusions are joint measurability,existence of this Gaussian pushforward probability kernel,and the exact same-noise output-difference representation with the stated averaged-Hessian properties and bounded linear remainder. They assert no invariant law,mixing or transport contraction,time-evolution result,expected evaluation count,proximal interpreter,additional independent Gaussian arrays or matrix certificate.
